\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; The main treatment for an ischemic stroke is a tissue plasminogen activator (tPA). It breaks up the blood clots that block blood flow to your brain. A healthcare provider will inject tPA into a vein in your arm. This type of medicine must be given within 3 hours after stroke symptoms start.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDrugs like\u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003Ealteplase, reteplase, and tenecteplase \u003C\/b\u003Ecan be used.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2)Fibronolytic therapy:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;streptokinase, anisoylated plasminogen-streptokinase activator complex, urokinase, and recombinant human tissue-type plasminogen activator. All 4 of these drugs activate the fibrinolytic system by converting plasminogen to the active enzyme, plasmin.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3) Dual antiplatelet therapy vs aspirin therapy:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; deep Reflexes - Lost\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Babinski's sign- Negative\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Clonus-Absent\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Paralysis-Flaccid.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Clasp Knife Reflex- Absent.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E7)Cushings triad:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;Cushing's triad refers to a set of signs that are indicative of increased intracranial pressure (ICP), or increased pressure in the brain.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECushing's triad consists of \u003Cb\u003Ebradycardia\u003C\/b\u003E (also known as a low heart rate), \u003Cb\u003Eirregular\u003C\/b\u003E \u003Cb\u003Erespirations\u003C\/b\u003E, and a \u003Cb\u003Ewidened pulse pressure\u003C\/b\u003E.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E8)Motor homonculus:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; The motor homunculus is a topographic representation of the body parts and its correspondents along the precentral gyrus of the frontal lobe. While the sensory homunculus is a topographic representation of the body parts along the postcentral gyrus of the parietal lobe.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELearning points:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1)Sudden onset of weakness or neurological deficit suggests - CEREBRO VASCULAR ACCIDENT.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2) Importance of proper clinical evaluation.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3) How to determine whether it is embolic or haemorrhagic or thrombotic stroke ?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; •Ischemic stroke : onset of symptoms usually noticed immediately after waking up from sleep\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; •Embolic or haemorrhagic stroke: onset of symptoms during activities\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; •Embolic stroke : history of cardiac diseases like RHD or Atrial fibrillation is present\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; • Haemorrhagic stroke: history of raised ICT - headache, nausea,vomiting etc.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E4) Use of CIMT:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;Constraint induced movement therapy or CIMT is a physiotherapy technique used to improve a person's upper limb function following neurological damage.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; itemprop=\"description articleBody\"\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;Greetings to\u0026nbsp;one and all going through my E log!!\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp; This is an online E log book to discuss our patient's de-identified health data shared after taking his\/her\/guardian's signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patient's problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs. This E log book also reflects my patient-centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"arial, sans-serif\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"arial, sans-serif\"\u003EA 44 yr old man , daily wage laborer R\/O Miryalaguda came to the OPD on 5th September 2023 with chief complaints of abdominal pain , vomitings and constipation and fever at nights\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003Esince 5 days.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 18 days back and then developed pain in the epigastric region and left hypochondriac region followed by high grade fever(at nights only = nocturnal), intermittent a\/o chills , one episode of vomiting daily morning contained food particles, bilious, non projectile, non blood tinged, odorless.\u0026nbsp;4 days later,\u0026nbsp;He got admitted in a local hospital and was diagnosed as\u0026nbsp;\u003Ci\u003EACUTE PANCREATITIS\u003C\/i\u003E\u0026nbsp;. and was discharged 2days later. Patient was advised to take few medications and Symptoms have completely disappeared in 4 days. Again After 4 days the patient developed pain abdomen similar to the previous episodes, stabbing type near epigastric region and left hypochondriac region, insidious onset, intermittent, gradually progressive , radiating to back. Pain aggravated on coughing. Similar episodes of vomitings occurred (one episode daily,\u0026nbsp;contained food particles, bilious, non projectile, non blood tinged, odorless) and had night raise in temperature (nocturnal fever) a\/o chills, intermittent, high grade and also had generalized body pains. He had c\/o constipation since 5 days. Flatus passed.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;No H\/O\u0026nbsp; loose stools, giddiness, polyuria, bleeding, dehydration, weight loss, oily stool, poor appetite, itchy skin, dark urine\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo H\/O chest pain, palpitations, SOB, Orthopnea, PND\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EH\/o Alcohol binge drinking since 25 years (one quarter = 180ml daily)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELast consumption August 21st 2023\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe wakes up at 6am ,has his breakfast by 7:30am and goes to work ,has his lunch by 1:30pm, takes alcohol (90 ml) ,returns home by around 6pm ,takes alcohol (90ml) ,has his dinner by around 9pm and goes to bed by 9:30pm.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cu\u003EStory from April 2023:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis 44 yr old man who is a known binge alcoholic since 25 yrs had c\/o pain abdomen (in epigastric area, stabbing type , gradually progressive, radiating to back) for a week, generalized body weakness, night fever a\/o chills and vomitings. He went to a local hospital where he was admitted for a week and given medications. At discharge, he was advised to stop alcohol consumption and take few medication (followed).\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAfter two months of abstinence, i.e; from\u0026nbsp;june 2023,\u0026nbsp;he started consuming alcohol (180 ml daily)\u0026nbsp;again\u0026nbsp;(no symptoms).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThree months passed away without any symptoms (on alcohol).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFrom August 18th 2023, he started developing pain abdomen in epigastric region and left hypochondriac area, stabbing type, gradually progressive, insidious, intermittent, radiating to back. He had raised temperature at nights a\/o chills (high grade). He had one episode of vomiting everyday in the morning (\u0026nbsp;contained food particles, bilious, non projectile, non blood tinged, odorless) . He also have c\/o generalized body pains and constipation.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOn August 22nd ,2023 he went to a local hospital and diagnosed with Acute Pancreatitis and Left minimal pleural effusion was admitted in hospital for 2 days and discharged. He was given a course of medications to be followed until 26th august. After completing the course, all his symptoms are resolved and he was asymptomatic for the next 4 days.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOn September 1st, he got his pain abdomen back , constipation (flatus passed), vomiting (one episode daily) a\/o fever and generalized weakness. He waited for 5 days thinking the symptoms would resolve and got admitted in KIMS, Narketpally on 5th September.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPAST HISTORY:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EN\/K\/C\/O DM, HTN, TB, Asthma, CAD, CVD,
